claims.text: The .npmrc diff adds a registry line pointing npm package downloads to http://127.0.0.1:4873/.
Rule-based detection classified the registry redirection as a hard signal and critical source change because it is not an approved registry.
The same .npmrc change was also flagged as a low-level sensitive-file change because it controls install/build behavior.
The redirect targets the loopback address 127.0.0.1 on port 4873, which is commonly used by a local package registry such as Verdaccio.

open_questions: Is http://127.0.0.1:4873/ expected to be available in CI, and would it serve vetted packages?
Was the local registry line intended to be committed, or should it be reverted/guarded in developer-local config?
Does the repository's policy allow any non-approved registry redirects, even loopback-only ones?
cases.summary: The PR adds registry=http://127.0.0.1:4873/ to .npmrc, redirecting package downloads to an unapproved local HTTP registry. This is a high-severity supply-chain configuration change, but the evidence does not show an external host, credential theft, or malicious package content.
cases.innocent_explanation: A developer may have pointed npm at a local Verdaccio-style registry on its default port for offline or pre-publication testing and committed the .npmrc line by accident.
